title: Retaking Toad Hall
text:
In Kenneth Grahame's The Wind in the Willows, the vain and reckless Toad was sent to prison for stealing a motorcar. While he was away, the weasels and stoats from the Wild Wood moved into his grand house, Toad Hall, and took it over. When Toad escaped and came home, they drove him off with a gun.

Toad wanted to charge in at once. His friends had a better plan. Badger revealed that he knew a secret underground passage, which ran from the riverbank right up into the butler's pantry of Toad Hall. And he had learned that the weasels were holding a banquet the next night to celebrate the Chief Weasel's birthday, when they would all be gathered in the dining hall, eating and drinking and off their guard.

Each friend took a job. Rat laid out a sword, a cudgel, pistols and a policeman's truncheon for each of them. Mole disguised himself as a washerwoman and went to the house, where he spread a rumor that a huge force was coming to attack from the river and the woods. The worried weasels sent their guards out to the edges of the grounds.

The next night the four friends crept through the tunnel, burst into the dining hall with sticks swinging and Badger roaring, and drove every weasel and stoat out of the house. Toad Hall was Toad's again.
lesson: Friends who plan together, each taking a part that suits them, can recover what one person's folly lost. Prepare carefully, and let the quiet ones do their share.
source: Kenneth Grahame, The Wind in the Willows (1908), chapters 11 and 12
